chunks: My father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from someone who narrated to him, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: If any of you lives far (from us) and there is a great distance between you and us, you should ascend to the highest place of your house, establish two Rak'ah of prayers, point toward our graves, and say Salām to us, for verily it will reach us.

key_terms.الشُّقَّةُ: The place of residence or dwelling

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform Ziyarah if they cannot visit the grave in person due to distance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the ritual of 'Ziyarat al-Qasirah' (short visitation) for those unable to travel, emphasizing the spiritual connectivity between the distant believer and the Ahl al-Bayt. By directing the visitor to face the specific graves of the Imams—particularly Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)—it underscores the Shia belief in the physical presence of the Imam’s soul receiving greetings, thereby transforming a local act of worship into a universal connection with the divine representatives.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father narrated to me from Sa’d, and from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from someone who narrated to him, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: If any of you lives far (from us) and there is a great distance between you and us, you should ascend to the highest place of your house, establish two Rak’ah of prayers, point toward our graves, and say Salām to us, for verily it will reach us.
